what_to_add: The learner's own example question, and it is under-taught. DRAFT: 'Anthropic introduced MCP on Nov 25 2024 as an open standard for connecting AI assistants to the systems where data lives. Before it, every new data source needed its own custom implementation, so each AI app had to wire each tool by hand (the N-apps x M-tools problem; this framing is ours, not Anthropic's wording). MCP replaces those fragmented integrations with one protocol: write a server once and any MCP client can use it. Anthropic released the spec and SDKs, local-server support in Claude Desktop and open-source reference servers. In Dec 2025 it donated MCP to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation to keep it vendor-neutral.' Also add Q3 (host/client/server; tools/list then tools/call over JSON-RPC), Q4 (open protocol vs per-vendor plugins; why split tools/resources/prompts by who controls them) and a diagram (N x M wires vs N + M via MCP).
